events.title: China Golden Week (National Day) travel vs spend
events.why_it_matters: Holiday volume is the live read on whether PBoC/mortgage support is thawing households, or whether property-scarred consumers still travel more and spend less.
events.what_to_watch: Official trips/revenue after Oct 7; per-capita spend vs 2025's ~911 yuan; outbound vs domestic mix.

events.title: California record heat wave / wildfire-smoke risk
events.why_it_matters: Late-season extreme heat lifts power demand and fire risk into SEMICON West week, a local but tradeable utilities/insurance overlay.
events.what_to_watch: Warnings through Oct 8, Bouquet Fire containment, and CAISO load/price spikes versus a Friday cooling trend.

events.title: September NFP miss: +29k, U3 4.2%, wages +3.0% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Payrolls badly missed ~+90k consensus, prior months were revised down, and wage growth slowed — collapsing October hike odds while leaving a growth-scare tail.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Oct 7 minutes and Oct 14 CPI confirm a hold, or energy CPI reopens the hike debate into the Oct 27–28 FOMC (just outside this window).

events.title: Eurozone September flash HICP 3.8% y/y (energy spike)
events.why_it_matters: Hottest headline since 2023, energy 18.8% y/y, tests the ECB's post-September 25 bp hike 'hold' into the Oct 29 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Final HICP on Oct 16 and whether core stays near 2.5% or services re-accelerate with energy.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November output targets unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core producers paused after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; actual barrels remain far below quotas because of the Iran war, so the signal is 'no extra supply'.
events.what_to_watch: Nov 1 eight-country follow-up and whether Saudi/Iraq actuals stay war-constrained even if quotas are unchanged.

events.title: Camp David Iran 'war council' after Hormuz rejection
events.why_it_matters: Senior US principals met as Iran restated Hormuz stays shut; raises odds of a military or sanctions step before US midterms rather than a 7-day reopen deal.
events.what_to_watch: Third-carrier/amphibious deployments, Yemen/Houthi track, and any White House decision after the closed-door session.

events.title: Tokyo September core CPI +2.7% y/y (hot lead for national CPI)
events.why_it_matters: Well above ~2.3% consensus after BoJ's Sept hike to 1.25%, keeping another hike in play at the Oct 29–30 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Oct 30 Outlook declares trend inflation at 2% and JGB/yen reaction into that meeting.

events.title: US August goods-and-services trade balance
events.why_it_matters: Deficit print is a read on tariff-front-running vs oil import bill after the truce extension.
events.what_to_watch: Goods deficit vs oil; China-related import volumes.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 earnings (jet-fuel stress test)
events.why_it_matters: Bellwether airline vs Brent >$100; Q3 plan assumed jet fuel ~$3.15/gal after a record $3.93 in Q2.
events.what_to_watch: Unit fuel, premium demand, Q4 margin guide, capacity cuts.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026 (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: Industry gathering as the sector crosses a $1tn revenue narrative; capex/tool commentary will be read against ASML/TSMC prints the same week.
events.what_to_watch: High-NA EUV, CoWoS/HBM tool demand, and China-export-control asides from equipment vendors.

events.title: September PPI and advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: PPI (~+0.5% m/m expected) is the pipeline into CPI/PCE; retail sales test whether $100 oil is already destroying goods demand after the NFP miss.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI vs control-group retail; gasoline-ex sales.

events.title: Eurozone September HICP final
events.why_it_matters: Confirms or revises the 3.8% flash that already challenged the ECB's measured hold.
events.what_to_watch: Revisions to energy/services; any core uptick from 2.5%.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure vs silicon-shield (no invasion priced as imminent)
events.why_it_matters: US sources still see full invasion unlikely near-term, but coast-guard quarantine tactics are the slow-burn risk to TSMC power/shipping — a chip-supply tail, not the base case.
events.what_to_watch: ADIZ/coast-guard counts; any arms-sale delay after the Trump–Xi summit.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: First activity print after Friday's +29k NFP miss; services are most of US GDP and test whether labor slowing is demand-wide or a hiring freeze.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~55.1–55.7 vs August 55.4; employment and prices-paid subindexes vs the growth-scare vs sticky-inflation split.

events.title: US–Iran war: Iran says Hormuz stays closed until US meets 7 conditions
events.why_it_matters: Seven-month war plus a contested Strait of Hormuz keeps a regime-level oil, shipping, and inflation premium in US and global risk assets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Tehran's seven Islamabad-memo conditions are met, escort/bypass flows, and any post–Camp David military step before midterms.

events.title: Brent holds ~$102 as Hormuz logistics, not just barrels, bite
events.why_it_matters: Crude transits have partially recovered via escorts/bypasses, but tanker rates, insurance, and refined-product tightness keep a consumer-tax and CPI input in place.
events.what_to_watch: Brent staying above $100, diesel/product cracks, and any resurgence of tanker attacks after last week's flow rebound.

events.title: China Golden Week travel vs spend
events.why_it_matters: Holiday volume is the live read on whether PBoC/mortgage support is thawing households, or whether property-scarred consumers still travel more and spend less.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 8 mainland reopen, full-week tourism revenue vs trip counts, and early retail/catering prints after the holiday.

events.title: US–China Busan truce extended to Jan 10, 2027
events.why_it_matters: Two-month extension past Nov 10 removes the near-term tariff cliff through holiday shipping, without resolving chips, EVs, or the 2027 expiry.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Board of Trade turns the pause into a broader deal, or talks stall into the January cliff.

events.title: US–China $60bn '30-for-30' tariff-relief lists
events.why_it_matters: Recommended MFN-style cuts on ~$30bn each way (US consumer goods vs China ag/energy/medical) would ease goods inflation and farm exports if implemented.
events.what_to_watch: Domestic legal implementation and start dates; chips, EVs, batteries, and soybeans remain excluded.

events.title: China factory PMI back above 50; PBoC PSL cut + mortgage subsidy
events.why_it_matters: Official manufacturing PMI 50.1 plus a 25 bp PSL cut, bigger relending quotas, and a 1 ppt first-home subsidy (from Oct 1) is the latest counter-cyclical push amid property drag.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Golden Week spending and Oct 19 activity data confirm the PMI bounce or show another property-led fade.

events.title: Korea September exports record $120.9bn, chips +263% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Semiconductor exports $60.3bn validate the AI-memory boom already signaled by Micron and keep Korea/Taiwan tech as a global growth engine even with $100 oil.
events.what_to_watch: Samsung Oct 8 prelims and TSMC Oct 15 for confirmation that HBM/foundry pricing is still accelerating.

events.title: Micron FQ4 beat and ~$61.5bn FQ1 revenue guide
events.why_it_matters: Memory pricing/AI capex confirmation is the strongest corporate offset to oil-and-tariff stagflation fears in the tape.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Samsung/TSMC/ASML prints this month ratify Micron's 86%+ GM and HBM-sold-out 2027 message.

events.title: FCC opens 12.7 GHz and 42 GHz for satellite broadband
events.why_it_matters: More than 1,000 MHz of new satellite-broadband spectrum is a multi-year capacity tailwind for LEO/broadband names, not a same-week tape mover.
events.what_to_watch: Federal Register effective dates, auction/licensing design, and incumbent-interference fights.

events.title: September FOMC minutes
events.why_it_matters: Markets need to know if the Sept 25 bp hike to 3.75–4.00% was a one-and-done into weak jobs, or if the committee still wanted more hikes against 3.7% PCE.
events.what_to_watch: Dissent language, inflation-upside vs labor-downside balance, and any hint that October is a hold (now ~17–20% hike odds).

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: First mega-cap consumer print of Q3 season; volumes vs price mix will show whether $100 oil and tariffs are hitting grocery demand.
events.what_to_watch: EPS vs ~$2.29–$2.30, North America volume, and FY guidance after a high-cost input quarter.

events.title: Samsung Electronics Q3 preliminary operating profit
events.why_it_matters: First Korea memory readout after Micron's blowout; a record OP print would confirm the AI-HBM supercycle is company-wide, not MU-specific.
events.what_to_watch: Prelim OP vs >100tn won forecasts and any commentary that DX/consumer is still the offset to memory strength.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Day-120 lockup tranche
events.why_it_matters: Up to ~328m shares become eligible 120 days after the June 12 IPO; supply overhang can spill into high-beta growth even if selling is not mandatory.
events.what_to_watch: Actual float vs eligible shares and whether the Oct 24/26 second tranche is already being positioned.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Airline bellwether for jet-fuel costs at $100+ Brent and for consumer/business travel demand after the labor miss.
events.what_to_watch: CASM-ex, fuel hedge/guide, and unit-revenue commentary versus ~$1.96 EPS consensus.

events.title: Q3 bank kickoff plus UNH and JNJ
events.why_it_matters: JPM/GS/C plus UNH/JNJ open earnings season on credit, NII, trading, and medical-cost trend — the cleanest read on whether stagflation is hitting loans or just headlines.
events.what_to_watch: NII/credit-card delinquencies, trading revenue, UNH medical-loss ratio, and any oil-shock commentary.

events.title: US existing-home sales (September)
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the rate-sensitive sector most exposed if 10-year yields stay elevated even as hike odds fall.
events.what_to_watch: Volumes vs pending-sales trend and median price; a miss would reinforce the growth-scare side of the NFP print.

events.title: US September CPI
events.why_it_matters: Headline is expected hot (~+0.5–0.6% m/m, ~3.7% y/y) on gasoline while core is seen cooling to ~+0.2% m/m — the print that decides if October is a hold or a re-hike scare.
events.what_to_watch: Gasoline/energy contribution vs core services; a hot core would fight the NFP-driven collapse in hike odds.

events.title: ASML Q3 plus BAC/MS/WFC/BLK
events.why_it_matters: ASML is the capex gate for AI foundry; same-day remaining megabanks complete the NII/credit mosaic after JPM.
events.what_to_watch: ASML 2027 demand/China mix vs ~$13.1bn sales consensus, and BAC/WFC consumer-credit quality.

events.title: US September PPI
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation after the energy shock; a hot PPI the day after CPI would keep the Fed from fully pivoting off the Sept hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and energy pass-through into intermediate goods versus the softer-core CPI narrative.

events.title: US September retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Demand-side check on whether households are still spending through $100 oil after the jobs miss; control-group sales feed Q3 GDP (Oct 29, outside window).
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs ex-auto/gas; a gasoline-inflated headline with weak real goods would be stagflationary.

events.title: TSMC Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Foundry bellwether for AI GPUs; guided $44.6–45.8bn revenue and 65–67% GM is the demand confirmation the whole semiconductor complex is priced on.
events.what_to_watch: N3/N2 mix, CoWoS, capex, and any China/export-control language versus the guide midpoint.

events.title: CIT supplemental briefs on global Section 301 forced-labor tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Duties covering ~99% of US imports (generally +10–12.5% from July 24) are in court; a vacatur would be a multi-sector inflation/margin shock in reverse.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 16 10,000-word briefs on statutory basis and standing after the Sept 30 oral argument; ruling date still unannounced.

events.title: Graham Act 30-day Russia/secondary-tariff clock
events.why_it_matters: Law signed Sept 18 requires up to 500% tariffs on Russian goods and up to 100% secondary tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil/gas / evasion facilitators — a binary trade shock if implemented at the cap.
events.what_to_watch: USTR/presidential notices around Oct 8 and the Oct 18 (Sunday) 30-day deadline; waivers, rate, and which 'top five' countries are named.

events.title: China September retail sales / activity cluster
events.why_it_matters: First hard activity print after Golden Week and the late-September easing package; August retail was already weak.
events.what_to_watch: Retail YoY vs the ~0.4% August run-rate, plus any accompanying industrial production/fixed-asset prints.

events.title: Europe aviation/ATC strike cluster
events.why_it_matters: Charleroi ATC, easyJet Portugal crew, and Italian transport actions are a niche traffic/cost overlay, not a market-wide shock.
events.what_to_watch: Whether actions spread into a wider October 14 Italian general strike or stay local.

top_risks: Hormuz stays shut or shipping attacks re-accelerate, keeping Brent ≥$100 and feeding US/EU headline CPI.
Graham Act secondary tariffs on Oct 18 hit top buyers of Russian oil (China and others), undoing the Busan truce's near-term calm.
September CPI prints a hot core, not just gasoline, forcing October FOMC hike odds back up after the NFP collapse.
CIT upholds July global Section 301 forced-labor duties, locking in a broad import-cost regime covering ~99% of US goods.
Camp David follow-through (third carrier / Yemen offensive) before midterms turns the Iran war from a logistics premium into a new kinetic leg.
top_opportunities: AI-memory/foundry complex (Micron already printed; Samsung Oct 8, ASML Oct 14, TSMC Oct 15, SEMICON West) remains the growth offset to $100 oil.
Busan truce through Jan 10 plus unimplemented 30-for-30 lists if paperwork actually cuts consumer-goods and ag tariffs.
Fed hold into Oct 27–28 is now the base case (~80%+) after +29k NFP; minutes Oct 7 can lock that in if they sound two-sided.
China policy easing (PSL, mortgage subsidy) plus a Golden Week spend beat would support EM/cyclicals into the Oct 19 data.
Energy producers and defense if OPEC+ stays on hold and Hormuz risk premium does not fade.
summary: The tape is still a two-factor regime: a live US–Iran war with Hormuz restricted and Brent near $102, versus a labor-market miss (+29k) that crushed October FOMC hike odds to ~20%. Policy is two-sided — a US–China truce to Jan 10 and $60bn relief lists cut the near-term China tariff cliff, while the Graham Act's Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff clock and the CIT challenge to global Section 301 duties keep trade risk binary. Q3 earnings open with PepsiCo then banks/UNH/ASML/TSMC against an AI-memory boom Korea and Micron have already validated.
